input.question: Why do spicy foods make your mouth feel hot temperature wise, and why do things like milk help it?
input.ground_truth: Capsaicin is the active ingredient in spicy food and it works by triggering the receptors for burning. Capsaicin is fat soluble so drinking milk, eating sour cream or guacamole helps dilute the capsaicin; drinking water is like throwing water on a grease fire -- it usually makes it worse.
